followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and the relevant capability scores.

**Task type:** Writing a job description is a neutral, transactional content-generation request. There's nothing harm-adjacent or ethically fraught here, so the preference dimensions where the models differ slightly (harm-adjacent content) aren't relevant. Both models report essentially equal, neutral preference for this kind of straightforward task.

**Capability:** Since neither model has a preference-based reason to favor it, I defaulted to the stronger performer. Dunlin-235B leads Lapwing-235B on every relevant metric — notably Creative Generation (84.7 vs 78.8, a ~6-point gap that exceeds the 2.0-point variance threshold) and general benchmarks like Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4). Drafting a job description draws on creative/composition skills, so that gap matters.

In short: equal fit, unequal capability — so I routed to the more capable model for the task family in question.
